newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian PM seeks new government partner.
newsitem.headline: Estonian PM seeks new government partner.

text.p: Estonian Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi looked for partners for a new government on Friday and pledged that the former Soviet country would keep on the path of economic reform.
Estonia, which quit the former Soviet Union in 1991, is heading for its seventh government since regaining independence.
Vaehi sought new partners after its junior partner, the Reform Party, walked out of the the government it had formed one year ago with the prime minister's Coalition Party.
The Reformists were furious over a pact Vaehi had made with a leading opposition party.
"A government led by me will not introduce any changes in the domestic, foreign or economic policies of Estonia," Vaehi told Reuters in an interview.
The Reform Party said Vaehi's agreement with the opposition Centre Party threatened to take Estonia too close to its huge neighbour Russia and slow down reforms.
Despite its political turbulence, Estonia has pushed on with an economic transformation that has put it among the leading reformers of former Communist states.
"The priorities which we have had will continue to top our agenda, including integration with western Europe, Baltic cooperation and normalising relations with Russia," Vaehi added.

Vaehi earlier accepted the resignation of Reform Party leader and foreign minister Siim Kallas and appointed former foreign minister Riivo Sinijaerv as caretaker in the post. Vaehi needs to fill five other cabinet jobs.
"I have started negotiations for setting up a governing coalition. These talks are not the simplest since the parliament is quite fractured," Vaehi said.
Vaehi, in alliance with a bloc of smaller rural parties, commands 40 seats in the 101-seat parliament.

Kallas was furious with Vaehi for signing the cooperation deal with the Centre Party, which Kallas said could lead to a situation where Estonia, the smallest of the Baltic states, became too friendly with Russia.
Suspicion of Russia runs deep in Estonia and many people believe it wants to reassert its influence over them.
Russia ruled Estonia and Baltic neighbours Latvia and Lithuania for most of the past 200 years and Balts resent the 50 years they spent as part of the former Soviet Union.
Observers now expect that Vaehi will try to forge a new coalition with the Centre Party, with which it ruled before the Reform Party coalition.
But it may have to invite in other parties and commentators have said he may even turn to the small Russian-language party.
The previous Coalition/Centre Party government collapsed amid scandal after Centre Party leader Edgar Savisaar was found to have taped confidential conversations with other politicians.
